results.finding: sections, unit counts and unit forms match the spec
Every blind outline summary agrees with the controlling idea of the aligned spec paragraph (p01-p46); the three intro callouts are house apparatus and align to none.

results.draft_locus: Who Acquires: A Difference of Degree, Country by Country ¶2
results.quote: Adyen's own acquiring also bounds some of its features.
results.finding: The outliner marked this unit two_ideas: the verdict on the slogan and what each company publishes, then a separate point that Adyen's own acquiring bounds features (network tokens, external American Express acquiring). The spec's p14 controlling idea itself joins the two; flow reader A also could not tell what the American Express clause adds.
Every unit serves one of S1-S5 through its section's advances_thesis; the in-person sentence in First Customers ¶1 is the documented cell the decision aid uses (changelog).

results.quote: And Adyen's update for the third quarter of 2026 says its Platforms offering "allows us to provide payments and financial products to smaller merchants, which will be a key driver of future growth."
results.finding: The Stripe quotation is explained ("in Europe Stripe rents that position from nobody"), but the Adyen quotation is left without its point: the text never says it contradicts "Adyen is for enterprises", and "Platforms" is not explained until the last bet. Both flow readers had to work out which quote answers which slogan.

results.quote: Behind the commercial slogan is a documented fact about beginnings.
results.finding: Declared cause_effect, carrying over 'a row that was a statement about packaging'. The opening sentence makes no link to the platform-or-suite section before it; it jumps back to the intro's slogan, so the boundary expresses no relationship. Both flow readers marked this section's position unclear.

results.draft_locus: Platforms: Who Stands Behind the Seller ¶1
results.quote: The last bet is also one of default, and it rests on the others.
results.finding: Declared additional_support carrying over 'Billing as a difference of sequence', but the spec's own 'introduces' says 'also one of default', so 'also' points back two sections to first customers rather than to billing. Both flow readers stumbled on the 'also'. The fault is in the spec's transition, which the draft follows.

results.quote: compares eight bets in a fixed order
results.finding: Both readers found the frame clear but could not find what orders the eight bets among themselves; the spec's large_to_small rationale (regulated base, then how products are made and packaged, then customer defaults, machines, and the product areas built on top) is never stated, so the roadmap announces only a 'fixed order'.
results.corroborated_by: flow reader B: 'What I could not find is the principle that orders the eight bets among themselves'

results.draft_locus: Who Runs the Machines: Own Infrastructure and a Public Cloud ¶1
results.quote: A pricing default can be changed by asking; the second difference of kind cannot.
results.finding: Both readers marked the hosting section's position unclear: naming it 'the second difference of kind' raises why it is not next to the first. The spec's rationale itself concedes the placement (open questions: 'hosting sits after the customer-facing defaults although it is a base-layer bet'), so the difficulty comes from the order.
results.corroborated_by: flow reader B: 'Who Runs the Machines: placed by contrast with pricing; why not next to the other difference of kind is unclear'

results.quote: Behind the commercial slogan is a documented fact about beginnings.
results.finding: Both readers marked the first-customers section's position unclear (it answers the commercial slogan but arrives fifth); the spec places it after how products are packaged and before the product areas that lean on it, but the prose gives no reason.
results.corroborated_by: flow reader B: 'First Customers and Today's Defaults: unclear. Answers the commercial slogan but arrives fifth'

results.draft_locus: Billing and Revenue Products: Built from 2018, Bought in 2026 ¶1
results.quote: Hosting cannot change for a customer; the seventh bet changed in 2026.
results.finding: Both readers marked billing's position unclear; reader A notes it retells the Orb purchase from Build or Buy. The spec's reason (billing depends on build-or-buy, as platforms depend on the license) is not said in the draft.
results.corroborated_by: flow reader B: 'Billing: placed by contrast with hosting; otherwise unclear'

results.draft_locus: One Platform or a Suite: Two Statements About Different Things ¶1

results.quote: Sorted by their evidence, the rows reduce to eight bets of three kinds.

Opens with a provocative quotation pair as the spec's hook; no weak pattern.
Conclusion sorts what is established, what depends and the author's position, then hands off; no mere restatement or new-material ending.

Established/Depends/Synthesis give the sorting (two of kind, the rest defaults and sequences) and the so-what (establish the kinds, negotiate the defaults; Questions to Ask turn it into the card's rows and its re-reading).
The author's synthesis returns to both opening slogans and rewrites each as a dated statement (the years used rely on Figure 2; recorded under flow_is_followable).

The intro reader listed all eight bets in the spec's order and the three kinds (kind; default, sequence or degree; not decidable), though unsure whether 'default, sequence or degree' is one kind; the prediction matches the roadmap.

The cold reader put billing, tax, usage, the blended default and self-serve defaults for A, in-person volume, Interchange++, European acquiring and the pre-financed sales-day payout for B, set billing aside for B and money-holding as minor for A, named realized prices, approval rates and volume per acquirer as unknowable, and rejected company size; matches expected.
The cold reader classed (1) and (4) as kind, (2) as degree, (3) as sequence/degree since 2026 and (5) as not decidable, each with a dated fact per company; matches expected.

results.quote: "Stripe is not a bank" (n.d.); e-money institutions in Ireland and the UK; US money transmitter; partner banks
results.finding: AC-3 requires every Stripe and Adyen cell to be a documented fact with its year or 'Not public'. In the money row the Stripe cell dates only the first fact; the e-money institutions, the US money-transmitter license (terms of November 2025) and the partner banks carry no year, though the map's lead says every cell repeats a fact 'with its year'. All other cells carry a year or n.d., and every reason is in an INFERENCE block or labeled as the author's reading.
